flagged.evidence: It says that “the only initial segment abc among cyclic conjugates starts at the first letter of r itself.” But the cyclic conjugate beginning at the fourth letter is abcxabc. Thus abc is an initial segment of both abcabcx=abc·abcx and abcxabc=abc·xabc; these give distinct ordered pairs in def-piece-in-a-symmetrised-presentation. The displayed abc is a piece, so this is not the claimed counterexample.

The step concludes “hence b^3=1 ... So G contains a nontrivial torsion element.” The equation b^3=1 alone permits b=1 and does not establish nontriviality. One must additionally identify the presentation with C3 or give a quotient onto C3.
The step says “so b^3=1. Thus G has nontrivial torsion.” As in the parallel false-statement item, b^3=1 does not itself prove b≠1. A quotient onto C3 or a Tietze elimination is required.

The Given hypothesis supplies only a null word w and a minimal-area diagram D. The cited Greendlinger result requires a reduced diagram with freely reduced, nontrivial boundary, but the proof establishes neither condition before asserting “[L1] gives a face.” After deletion, step 2.1 repeats the assertion without showing the new diagram is reduced or has freely reduced boundary. This unsupported iteration is the core of the area bound.

No nontriviality condition on the torsion element, nor nonempty-relator condition, is stated. For the empty relator set, the presentation ⟨x | ∅⟩ is vacuously symmetrised C'(1/6); its identity has finite order, but there is no defining relator whose root can occur in the claimed conclusion. The proof likewise only assumes “some n≥1 satisfies u^n=1,” which includes the identity.

The cited Greendlinger lemma gives only a face with an outer arc longer than half its perimeter. The proof then says “Standard periodic-overlap cancellation then forces the relator ... to be a proper power ... and the boundary word u to be conjugate to a power” without a supplied lemma or argument connecting repetition on u^n to a second occurrence in that relator. This is the essential torsion-theorem inference, not a consequence stated by [L1].
The summary says “the standard completions of a finite group and of $mathbb Z$”. The command is missing its backslash, so the mathematical expression is malformed.

After setting M=N1∩⋯∩Nm, the proof says “the element g1 can be adjusted inside its M-coset so that its image in each quotient ... equals the prescribed coordinate.” Since M⊆Nk, every element of g1M has the same image g1Nk, so such adjustment cannot change any prescribed coordinate. A valid proof must use a representative of the compatible M-coordinate of a nonempty cylinder.

The asserted second equivalence omits compactness. Z with its profinite topology has the neighbourhood basis nZ of open normal subgroups and each quotient Z/nZ is finite, yet it is not profinite: its canonical image is a proper dense nonclosed subspace of its compact completion. Thus the open-normal finite-quotient basis condition alone does not characterize profinite groups.

The proof obtains a finite quotient of ker(ρ), then claims that “Pulling back the corresponding kernel gives a finite-index subgroup K′≤K containing H but not g.” A quotient of ker(ρ) provides no homomorphism from K to that quotient, and its kernel need not be invariant under conjugation by H; hence there is no stated pullback subgroup of K containing H. The cited residual finiteness does not supply this required separation construction.

Step 1.1 establishes at most that an existing compatible tuple is determined by its i0-coordinate. Step 2.1 then calls the projection bijective without proving that every element of Gi0 extends to a compatible tuple, including coordinates not comparable with i0. That existence construction is absent.
